challenge.method: Reacquired all seven pinned originals in the requested order, inspected the loader, CLI and renderer, and compared their behavior with the two dated receipts. Invoked the fixed reproduction once in fresh scratch. Its checks exercised modified input, zero and duplicate placeholders, partial and invalid substitutions, unfilled and filled previews, a real write and an existing-target attempt. Compared the checked file's length and digest with the byte splice and with both historical measurements.
challenge.results: The CLI refused the modified input at digest verification. Direct renderer checks refused zero and duplicate notice matches. The CLI also refused a partial holder/year pair, an invalid year and a multiline holder. An unfilled preview returned the template, and a filled preview produced the rendered bytes without installing a file. An existing destination blocked the unforced write. These results disconfirm broader claims that arbitrary inputs work, that a preview proves installation, or that an existing file is overwritten by default. The separate exact-write check succeeded on a new target. Its measured digest matched the claim. No challenge contradicted the scoped write.

limitations: This assessment uses the supplied SCES-1.0 designation, commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710 and bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce. The seven named source acquisitions did not include the policy bundle itself.
The finding covers the pinned implementation, SPDX bytes, runtime, fixture arguments and fresh scratch destination. Other inputs, destinations, platforms and revisions require separate evidence.

The two historical receipts and the replay share the same upstream implementation, SPDX sources and method. They demonstrate repeatability of one specimen and supply no additional original authority for the license text.
Legal authority to apply the license, retention of notices in another project and rights to redistribute the SPDX input are outside the observation.
